AI.result: StreamEgo achieves generalizable, unbounded real-time streaming Exo2Ego video generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.
AI.conclusion: Dual-branch kinematic priors and chunk-wise autoregressive distillation enable live, high-quality exocentric-to-egocentric video translation.

title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?
summary: Spatial intelligence requires agents to acquire visual evidence and integrate partial observations into coherent three-dimensional representations. We introduce SpatialScout-V2, which extends SpatialScout's active mapping task from simulation to real residential scenes through three advances: real visual observations, preservation of original scene content, and interactive exploration of recorded views. Built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, the benchmark covers 3,171 target objects across 29 categories. Given a fixed target inventory, agents autonomously select recorded viewpoints and viewing directions, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively estimate and revise object centers within a fixed interaction budget. We evaluate the localization accuracy and completeness of object-center maps using mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models (VLMs), we find that six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20\%. Even the best-performing model, Claude Opus 5.5, reaches only 22.52\%, with just 18.36\% of targets exceeding an IoU of 0.5. Further analysis shows that broad submission coverage can coexist with limited localization accuracy, while target omissions further reduce overall scores. These results highlight substantial challenges in constructing accurate and complete object-center maps through active exploration of real scenes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SpatialScout-V2, a real-world active 3D scene exploration benchmark built from 100 homes in Realsee3D, showing that frontier VLMs achieve at most 22.52% mean IoU on object-center localization.
AI.motivation: Active 3D mapping benchmarks have largely been limited to simulation, leaving it unclear how well VLM agents explore real-world scenes and integrate partial observations.
AI.method: SpatialScout-V2 comprises 3,171 target objects across 29 categories in 100 real homes from Realsee3D, requiring agents to select viewpoints and viewing directions within an interaction budget to estimate and revise object centers, evaluated by mean IoU, IoU-threshold hit rates, and target coverage.
AI.result: Across seven frontier VLMs, six achieve an all-target mean IoU below 20%, and the best model (Claude Opus 5.5) reaches only 22.52% mean IoU with 18.36% of targets exceeding 0.5 IoU.
AI.conclusion: Frontier VLMs still face major challenges in active exploration, viewpoint integration, and accurate 3D object-center localization in real residential environments.

title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
summary: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes FlexVSR, a continuous-scale streaming generative video super-resolution framework that adapts a frozen DiT prior using a lightweight 0.274M-parameter latent adapter.
AI.motivation: Extending fixed-scale generative VSR to arbitrary target scales either wastes compute via downsampling or requires costly re-optimization of the diffusion transformer (DiT).
AI.method: FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a 0.274M-parameter latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before entering a frozen VSR DiT, trained with supervision at only a few scales while preserving causal streaming.
AI.result: With an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, FlexVSR achieves competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming and offline baselines, and strong generalization to unseen continuous scales.
AI.conclusion: Scale-aware adaptation at the latent interface enables continuous-scale real-time streaming generative VSR without modifying the underlying DiT prior.

title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
summary: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we first train the VLM to select an action suited to the current region through step-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), using preferences derived from immediate restoration feedback to supervise only the differing component in each action pair. To account for the effects of current actions on subsequent restoration, we then apply trajectory-level DPO, using preferences derived from complete trajectory scores to supervise the sole differing action in each trajectory pair. Furthermore, as conventional image-pair datasets do not directly provide preferences over regional restoration decisions, we construct a regional restoration preference dataset comprising 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs for two-stage VLM training. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single degradations. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of two-stage preference learning in improving restoration quality.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes RegionAgent, a VLM-based regional image restoration framework trained with two-stage step-level and trajectory-level DPO on a new regional preference dataset.
AI.motivation: Images with non-uniform coupled degradations require distinct, sequential regional restoration actions, whereas existing methods apply globally uniform operations that cause incomplete restoration or content damage.
AI.method: RegionAgent trains a VLM to select region-specific restoration actions iteratively using step-level DPO from immediate feedback followed by trajectory-level DPO from complete trajectory scores, supported by a constructed dataset of 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single degradations, with ablations validating the two-stage preference learning.
AI.conclusion: Two-stage step- and trajectory-level preference optimization enables VLMs to plan sequential, region-aware restoration actions for complex coupled degradations.

title: Backbone Matters: Benchmarking Encoder-Decoder Networks for Semantic Segmentation of Driving Scenes on BDD100K
summary: Semantic segmentation gives an autonomous vehicle a dense, pixel-level description of its surroundings and is a core part of scene understanding. Most segmentation networks consist of an encoder (the backbone) and a decoder, yet the backbone is often chosen without a systematic comparison. This work studies this choice on the BDD100K driving dataset. Four widely used decoders (U-Net, FPN, LinkNet and PSPNet) are combined with 13 backbones from six families (ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, Inception, MobileNet and EfficientNet), and all 52 models are trained with one common protocol. The best model, an FPN decoder with an EfficientNet-B4 backbone, reaches 62.6% mean intersection over union (mIoU), 89.8% accuracy and a loss of 0.092. Only two of the 52 models, both FPN with EfficientNet, exceed the 56.9% mIoU reported with the BDD100K benchmark. The effect of the backbone depends strongly on the decoder: the same EfficientNet-B4 gives 42.6% mIoU with PSPNet but 62.6% with FPN, and the gap between the best and the worst backbone ranges from 12.0 points (U-Net) to 42.5 points (FPN). The results and the scope of this study are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks 52 encoder-decoder combinations (4 decoders and 13 backbones) on BDD100K semantic segmentation, finding that FPN with EfficientNet-B4 performs best at 62.6% mIoU.
AI.motivation: Segmentation backbones are often chosen without systematic comparison, leaving the interaction between encoder family and decoder architecture unclear.
AI.method: The authors combine four decoders (U-Net, FPN, LinkNet, PSPNet) with 13 backbones across six families (ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, Inception, MobileNet, EfficientNet) and train all 52 models under a unified protocol on BDD100K.
AI.result: FPN with EfficientNet-B4 achieves the best performance (62.6% mIoU, 89.8% accuracy, 0.092 loss), only two models (both FPN with EfficientNet) beat the 56.9% BDD100K benchmark, and backbone impact varies strongly by decoder (12.0 mIoU range for U-Net vs. 42.5 for FPN; EfficientNet-B4 drops to 42.6% with PSPNet).
AI.conclusion: Encoder performance in semantic segmentation is heavily dependent on the paired decoder architecture, underscoring the need for joint encoder-decoder evaluation.

title: A version of the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition for full/quad pol synthetic aperture radar data
summary: Based on the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition of reflection symmetric polarimetric SAR data we present a version for full/quad polarisation data. We demonstrate both versions on X-band F-SAR data over Vejers, Denmark. Differences between the original and our version of the decomposition occur especially for very bright man-made targets. These differences come with lower entropy for our version giving an improved focus on a more pronounced dominant scattering mechanism for these objects. Interpretation of the scattering mechanism related to the full/quad pol version of the decomposition is facilitated by means of the Cloude/Pottier $\bar{\alpha}$ angle.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition from reflection-symmetric to full/quad-polarization SAR data, yielding lower entropy and sharper dominant scattering mechanisms on bright man-made targets.
AI.motivation: The standard Cloude/van Zyl decomposition assumes reflection-symmetric polarimetric SAR data, limiting its applicability to full/quad-polarization observations.
AI.method: The authors formulate a full/quad-polarization version of the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition and interpret its scattering mechanisms using the Cloude/Pottier $\bar{\alpha}$ angle on X-band F-SAR data over Vejers, Denmark.
AI.result: Compared to the original decomposition, the full/quad-polarization version exhibits lower entropy and a more pronounced dominant scattering mechanism, particularly for bright man-made targets.
AI.conclusion: Extending the Cloude/van Zyl decomposition to full/quad-polarization data improves scattering mechanism discrimination for complex man-made targets in SAR imagery.

title: SpecWM: Turning Verification into Refinement for Streaming World Models
summary: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. Existing speculative methods combine their strengths through fast draft generation and selective target regeneration guided by rewards on decoded frames. However, verification covers only the external scorer's evaluation dimensions and adds decoding and scoring costs. Moreover, these scores provide no correction, requiring costly target regeneration for rejected drafts. To address these limitations, we propose Speculative World Model (SpecWM), a unified, training-free inference framework for streaming world models. It verifies draft chunks using the target's latent velocity field. Verification also yields a reusable correction; two thresholds select Accept, Refine, or Reject. Specifically, one-step refinement reuses it to improve perceptual quality, while three-step refinement strengthens camera following and trajectory consistency. These findings motivate transition-aware refinement. On WBench Navigation, SpecWM improves visual quality at 1.63$\times$ speedup over the target and raises NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, achieving the best quality-speed-control trade-off. Additionally, our LongSpecBench shows sustained quality and control over long, multi-turn rollouts, while experiments on Hy-Nomas validate SpecWM across backbones and denoising budgets.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes SpecWM, a training-free speculative inference framework for streaming world models that verifies and reuses target latent velocity corrections, achieving a 1.63x speedup on WBench Navigation.
AI.motivation: Existing speculative world model methods rely on costly frame decoding and external reward scoring for verification and discard rejected drafts without providing corrections.
AI.method: SpecWM verifies draft chunks directly using the target model's latent velocity field and reuses the resulting correction via two thresholds to Accept, Refine (1-step for perceptual quality or 3-step for camera/trajectory consistency), or Reject.
AI.result: On WBench Navigation, SpecWM achieves a 1.63x speedup over the target model while improving visual quality and raising NavScore from the draft's 75.99 to 85.63, and sustains quality over long rollouts on LongSpecBench.
AI.conclusion: Turning latent velocity verification into reusable multi-step refinement provides a superior quality-speed-control trade-off for streaming world models.

title: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers
summary: Humanoid agents in everyday environments are expected to react to diverse cues as humans do, with semantically appropriate and physically executable behaviors. Existing cue-driven reaction generation methods support only a narrow range of cue modalities and are limited to purely kinematic generation, leaving the resulting reactions susceptible to physical artifacts. To this end, we present MixReact, the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues, integrating a Discrete--Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for physical execution. DisCo-MoT couples a discrete masked-modeling branch with a continuous autoregressive diffusion branch via one-way mixture attention within a MoT architecture. Guidance from discrete context mitigates collapse into averaged behaviors in one-to-many reaction generation, while direct prediction in continuous state space bypasses the decoding bottleneck of discrete representations. HAT then maps the predicted next state and observed execution history to executable actions, enabling robust closed-loop control in physics-based simulation. Experiments across all three modalities demonstrate consistent improvements over the baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, while ablations validate the complementary contributions of the components. Our code will be released to facilitate future research. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: This paper presents MixReact, a unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues using a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers and a History-aware Action Transformer.
AI.motivation: Existing cue-driven reaction generation methods support limited modalities and produce purely kinematic motions that suffer from physical artifacts.
AI.method: MixReact pairs a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT)—coupling a discrete masked-modeling branch with a continuous autoregressive diffusion branch via one-way mixture attention—with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for closed-loop physical execution.
AI.result: Experiments across text, audio, and video cues demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, with ablations confirming each component's contribution.
AI.conclusion: Combining discrete-continuous mixture state prediction with history-aware action execution enables physically executable, multimodal reactive humanoid control.

title: Attention Drift Regularization with Adaptive Initialization for Domain-Robust Visual Recognition
summary: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained source model to unlabeled target domains without source data access, yet two critical failure modes remain unaddressed. First, attention drift: source-learned attention maps shift toward spurious or background features under distribution shift, destabilizing feature representations. Second, domain-gap-agnostic initialization: applying a single fixed source model uniformly across all target domains ignores domain gap severity, causing premature overfitting to noisy pseudo-labels under large shifts. We propose DGA-CAFC to address both failures. The Counterfactual Attention-based Feature Consistency (CAFC) module enforces feature stability by minimizing the discrepancy between representations computed under learned attention and those under counterfactual-inspired normalized perturbations, thereby promoting domain-robust features independent of spurious attention shifts. The Domain-Gap Aware Source Model Selection (DGASS) module estimates domain gap severity via target prediction entropy and selects the source model variant whose confidence level best matches the estimated gap, reducing negative transfer and stabilizing pseudo-label quality. Crucially, CAFC transfers beyond SFDA: applied as a lightweight regularizer to standard domain generalization objectives without target data. Extensive experiments across SFDA and DG benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently improves over recent baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of the proposed framework. Project page is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: This paper proposes DGA-CAFC for source-free domain adaptation and domain generalization, combining counterfactual attention feature consistency with domain-gap-aware source model selection.
AI.motivation: Source-free domain adaptation suffers from attention drift toward spurious background features under distribution shift and domain-gap-agnostic initialization that overfits to noisy pseudo-labels.
AI.method: DGA-CAFC introduces Counterfactual Attention-based Feature Consistency (CAFC) to stabilize representations under counterfactual attention perturbations, and Domain-Gap Aware Source Model Selection (DGASS) to estimate domain gap via target prediction entropy and select a matching source model variant.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across source-free domain adaptation and domain generalization benchmarks show consistent improvements over recent baselines, with CAFC also transferring as a lightweight regularizer without target data.
AI.conclusion: Regularizing attention drift and matching source model initialization to estimated domain gap substantially improves domain-robust visual recognition.

title: Beyond Covers and Titles: Evidence-First Ranking for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
summary: Short-video platforms rank new uploads before anyone has watched them, using content towers that read a video's cover, title and frames. Existing attacks on content-aware recommenders perturb pixels or features and ignore platform re-encoding, and existing defenses train against norm-bounded perturbations that neither match real edits nor preserve recommendation quality. We show with REAP, a realizable attack through {a simulated platform channel (H.264 transcoding, rescaling, cropping and JPEG)}, that packaging edits raise a cold video by 32.0 rank-percentile points in unrelated audiences. We then observe that cold-start ranking does not need the packaging at all: a tower that sees only the video body ranks cold items best. Building on this, we propose Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which scores cold videos from their body, admits packaging only through a support-gated residual bounded by $\gamma$, and merges cold and warm rankings by rank percentile, yielding an exact certificate against any packaging edit. On MicroLens-100K, EFR cuts the attack gain by 81% and raises cold-start Recall@100 from 0.1133 to 0.170, while keeping the merged NDCG@10 within 4% of the undefended system.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that packaging edits can manipulate cold-start video rankings by 32.0 percentile points and proposes Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which cuts attack gains by 81% on MicroLens-100K.
AI.motivation: Short-video cold-start recommenders rely on covers and titles that can be manipulated, while existing defenses ignore platform re-encoding and degrade recommendation quality.
AI.method: The authors demonstrate the realizable REAP attack through a simulated platform channel (H.264 transcoding, rescaling, cropping, JPEG) and propose Evidence-First Ranking (EFR), which scores cold videos from their video body, bounds packaging via a support-gated residual $\gamma$, and merges cold and warm rankings by percentile.
AI.result: REAP raises cold-video rank by 32.0 percentile points in unrelated audiences; on MicroLens-100K, EFR cuts attack gain by 81%, raises cold-start Recall@100 from 0.1133 to 0.170, and keeps merged NDCG@10 within 4% of the undefended system.
AI.conclusion: Scoring cold-start videos primarily from body content with bounded packaging residuals provides a certified defense against packaging manipulation while improving cold-start recall.

title: Prism: Hierarchical Text Detection with Minimalist Design
summary: Hierarchical text detection aims to localize words, text lines, and paragraphs while parsing their structural relationships. It provides essential structural cues for visual text understanding. To maximize accuracy, existing methods typically rely on complex multi-scale feature fusion necks and heavy-weight heads, resulting in bloated architectures and low inference efficiency. In this paper, we argue that a sufficiently pre-trained backbone can effectively replace these sophisticated external modules, while simple geometric inclusion suffices for hierarchical text structural parsing. Thus, we propose Prism, a minimalist framework for hierarchical text detection. Prism performs multi-granularity detection by attaching parallel lightweight heads to a single-scale backbone feature map, covering words, text lines, and paragraphs, and reconstructs the structural hierarchy via an efficient geometric inclusion algorithm. In addition, we systematically compare representative lightweight head archetypes and show that pixel-level regression offers the best accuracy-efficiency trade-off in this setting. Experiments on multiple public benchmarks show that our significantly simplified architecture achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with remarkable efficiency. Specifically, it runs $1.7\times$ faster than LRANet on CTW1500 while achieving higher accuracy, and surpasses the current SOTA method, OmniParser V2, by over 6 PQ points on the hierarchical HierText dataset. Code will be released soon.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Prism, a minimalist hierarchical text detection framework using parallel lightweight heads on a single-scale backbone and geometric inclusion, running 1.7x faster than LRANet on CTW1500.
AI.motivation: Existing hierarchical text detectors rely on complex multi-scale feature fusion necks and heavy heads, resulting in bloated architectures and slow inference.
AI.method: Prism attaches parallel lightweight pixel-level regression heads to a single-scale pretrained backbone to detect words, text lines, and paragraphs, and reconstructs the hierarchy using a geometric inclusion algorithm.
AI.result: Prism runs 1.7x faster than LRANet on CTW1500 with higher accuracy and surpasses OmniParser V2 by over 6 PQ points on the hierarchical HierText dataset.
AI.conclusion: A strong pretrained single-scale backbone with lightweight pixel-level regression heads and geometric inclusion suffices for fast, state-of-the-art hierarchical text detection.

title: Digitization of Analogue Gauges using Computer Vision
summary: Analogue gauges remain prevalent in manufacturing industries for measuring physical quantities, yet manual monitoring by operators introduces human error and operational inefficiency. This research developed and evaluated an automated gauge reading system using computer vision and deep learning techniques. Three hybrid approaches were implemented and compared: OpenCV with Scikit-Image (traditional computer vision), OpenCV with ResNet18, and OpenCV with VGG19 (deep learning approaches). A comprehensive dataset of 1,848 pressure gauge images (0-10 BAR range) was curated through web scraping, synthetic generation, and augmentation techniques. The experimental results demonstrate that ResNet18 significantly outperforms the alternatives, achieving an accuracy of 97.3%, compared to VGG19's 64.4% and Scikit-Image's 63.8%. The study validates the effectiveness of residual learning architectures for industrial gauge digitization, providing a robust foundation for Industry 5.0 automation applications.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates three computer vision pipelines for reading analogue pressure gauges on a curated 1,848-image dataset, finding that OpenCV with ResNet18 achieves 97.3% accuracy.
AI.motivation: Manual monitoring of analogue gauges in manufacturing introduces human error and operational inefficiency.
AI.method: The authors curate 1,848 pressure gauge images (0-10 BAR) via web scraping, synthetic generation, and augmentation, and compare OpenCV paired with Scikit-Image, ResNet18, and VGG19.
AI.result: OpenCV with ResNet18 achieves 97.3% accuracy, substantially outperforming OpenCV with VGG19 (64.4%) and OpenCV with Scikit-Image (63.8%).
AI.conclusion: Residual learning paired with OpenCV preprocessing provides an accurate, reliable foundation for automated industrial analogue gauge digitization.

title: Tracking Objects Through Assembly and Decomposition
summary: Tracking objects through transformations is essential for understanding real-world dynamics. Recent work has extended traditional object tracking to detect state changes. However, existing methods require an initial object prompt and detect only its decompositions, missing assembly events, which begin with multiple objects rather than one. We therefore introduce a prompt-free formulation of this task, where the goal is to recover all object tracks and detect both decomposition and assembly events given only a video. Our key insight is that assembly is decomposition in reverse. Building on this insight, we present Atlas, a zero-shot system that constructs and jointly reasons over forward and reverse spatiotemporal partitions to recover object tracks and their transformations. We further introduce OmniST, a benchmark with dense annotations of objects and both transformation types. On OmniST, Atlas recovers more than twice as many state changes as prior methods while remaining competitive on existing benchmarks that only evaluate decomposition.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a prompt-free formulation for tracking objects through both decomposition and assembly, presenting the zero-shot Atlas system and the OmniST benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing state-change tracking methods require an initial object prompt and only detect decompositions, missing assembly events that start from multiple objects.
AI.method: Exploiting the insight that assembly is decomposition in reverse, Atlas constructs and jointly reasons over forward and reverse spatiotemporal partitions in a zero-shot manner to recover all object tracks and both transformation types, evaluated on the new densely annotated OmniST benchmark.
AI.result: On OmniST, Atlas recovers more than twice as many state changes as prior methods while remaining competitive on existing decomposition-only benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Joint forward-reverse spatiotemporal reasoning enables prompt-free tracking of both assembly and decomposition events in complex dynamic scenes.

title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
summary: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. However, most pathology foundation models are trained on tissue patches and capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either restricted to specific cell populations or rely on computationally expensive architectures with hundreds of millions of parameters. Applying ViTs directly to small cellular crops also presents an architectural challenge: upsampling increases computational cost without adding morphological information and may introduce interpolation artefacts. To address these limitations, we introduce C-LiTE, a lightweight foundation model for cellular representation learning in H&E-stained histopathology, with only 22 million parameters. C-LiTE employs a native-resolution tokenisation strategy tailored to cellular inputs, processing 64 x 64 px cell-centred crops using a 4 x 4 patch embedding to produce a 16 x 16 token grid without image upsampling. To transfer visual knowledge from large-scale pre-training, we adapt the patch embedding weights of a pre-trained ViT-5-S using a pseudoinverse-based transformation, enabling weight initialisation at the finer patch resolution. We further assemble a pre-training dataset of 60 million cell-centred crops from TCGA, balanced across 19 cancer types and 16 tissue types. To our knowledge, this represents the largest public dataset for self-supervised pre-training on H&E images at the cellular level. We evaluate C-LiTE on seven public datasets spanning mitotic figure recognition, nucleus and cell-type classification, and immune cell phenotyping. Under frozen-feature evaluation, C-LiTE achieves a mean macro-F1 of 0.670, approaching CytoFormer (0.682) with approximately 30x fewer parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents C-LiTE, a 22M-parameter cellular foundation model for H&E histopathology trained on 60 million cell-centred crops, approaching CytoFormer's accuracy with 30x fewer parameters.
AI.motivation: Tissue-patch pathology foundation models capture cellular features only implicitly, while existing cell-level models are either narrow in scope or rely on heavy architectures and upsampling that introduces interpolation artifacts.
AI.method: C-LiTE tokenizes 64x64 px cell-centred crops at native resolution using 4x4 patch embeddings, initializes weights from a pretrained ViT-5-S via a pseudoinverse-based transformation, and pretrains self-supervised on 60 million TCGA cell crops across 19 cancer and 16 tissue types.
AI.result: Across seven public cellular classification and phenotyping datasets under frozen-feature evaluation, C-LiTE achieves a mean macro-F1 of 0.670, approaching CytoFormer (0.682) with approximately 30x fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: Native-resolution tokenization and large-scale cell-centred pretraining enable compact, parameter-efficient foundation models for computational pathology.

title: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning
summary: Agentic visual reasoning improves vision-language models by selectively enlarging evidence without adding new scene content, but the benefit depends on whether fine structure remains accessible and whether local observations stay grounded in the full scene. We identify three recurring bottlenecks: high-frequency detail can be attenuated during visual-token formation; spatially distributed evidence can remain encoded yet difficult for the language model to retrieve; and isolated crops can weaken whole-detail correspondence through scale and positional mismatch. ResVision addresses these limitations with two complementary components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) estimates image complexity and selects an adaptive global sampling scale, avoiding unnecessary enlargement on simple inputs while allocating more visual tokens to detail-rich images. Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view, preserving local detail and global context across tool turns. We evaluate Direct and Agentic variants on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks spanning six visual-reasoning families. Complete ResVision (Agentic Base plus SMR plus CPI) is best for every model, improving by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base. These results show that adaptive visual sampling and context-preserving inspection address distinct, complementary constraints in multimodal reasoning.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes ResVision, combining Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection, to improve agentic VLM visual reasoning by 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base across 29 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Agentic visual reasoning can suffer from high-frequency detail attenuation during tokenization, difficulty retrieving spatially distributed evidence, and scale/positional mismatch in isolated crops.
AI.method: ResVision introduces Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) to adaptively allocate visual tokens based on estimated image complexity, and Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) to return each inspected crop alongside the complete working view across tool turns.
AI.result: Evaluated on four frontier VLMs across 29 benchmarks, complete ResVision improves by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive complexity-based visual sampling and context-preserving crop inspection address complementary bottlenecks in multimodal agentic visual reasoning.
